source.title: The Spectrum of Fisher Information of Deep Networks Achieving Dynamical Isometry

record.file_problem: none; full paper text and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures training dynamics under learning-rate and depth sweeps, then compares observed accuracy and loss boundaries with a theoretical stability boundary. It does not reproduce the specific above-threshold recovery recipe in V5.
record.gate_note: The paper's FIM spectrum results and references to prior work on dynamical isometry are not rows. Figure 4/5 learning-rate and depth sweeps are rows because they report this study's training outcomes. Initialization, normalization, and shortcut comparisons are not tested.
record.test_reason: The study reports reduced training MSE beyond the initial linearized stability boundary and shrinking conditional FIM spectra after training. These bear on components of V5 through online gradient descent, although the full recovery trajectory is not measured.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct: under approximate dynamical isometry, nonzero conditional FIM eigenvalues concentrate near a maximum growing linearly with depth, motivating an inverse-depth learning-rate scale. Accuracy boundaries agree with this prediction, while some above-boundary runs show reduced loss and changed spectra. The authors do not establish the full catapult trajectory.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies online gradient descent on small fixed subsets of Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR10 while sweeping learning rate and depth, under hard-tanh settings chosen for approximate dynamical isometry. It does not use the stated wide-network squared-loss training recipe or report the transient loss-rise sequence.
record.method_sensitivity: Learning-rate and depth sweeps; dataset and train versus test evaluation change the reported outcome. CIFAR10 shows a larger train-test accuracy difference than Fashion-MNIST. Above the stated boundary, loss reduction does not correspond to improved accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Training and testing accuracy collapse approximately along η = 2/L; accuracy does not improve in the region where loss decreases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under this dynamical-isometry recipe, the learning-rate scale for successful classification decreases inversely with depth.

fits_no_version.finding: Testing MSE can remain modest beyond the initial stability boundary.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Endpoint testing loss can violate the initial linearized stability prediction in these online-training experiments.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics (AISTATS 2021), PMLR Volume 130
record.problems: Training uses only 500 examples, with one epoch for Fashion-MNIST and ten for CIFAR10. The paper notes overfitting on the small CIFAR10 training set. The training-dynamics results are heatmaps without numeric cell values in the text; the Appendix B text has an apparent η > L/2 versus η > 2/L inconsistency.

untested.parts: Convolutional networks reaching near-zero training classification error, random labels, and model-size or regularization comparisons.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious minima, and extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation in plain convolutional networks and comparisons with identity shortcuts or alternative initialization recipes.
Whether different initialization methods change training speed or trainable depth; all training experiments use the same dynamical-isometry recipe.

A transient loss rise followed by low training loss; a measured range of larger rates causing divergence; full-batch sharpness tracking at the stability threshold; and divergence from initially subthreshold rates.
Batch-normalization comparisons and Fixup's speed and stability without normalization.

missing.what: Conditional FIM eigenvalue distributions shrink after 500 Fashion-MNIST training steps in most examined regions above η = 2/L. Add a separate result row comparing the post-training spectrum with initialization; this measures a FIM proxy for curvature, not the exact loss Hessian.

record.verdict_notes: Unimproved classification accuracy does not limit V5, which concerns loss. Missing temporal measurements are untested components, not evidence against recovery. Figures are represented only by extracted text, so numerical heatmap values cannot be verified.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error to zero or near zero, including on corrupted or random labels; model size, optimizer, and early stopping.
Student-teacher ReLU problems, spurious minima, and width changes.
Plain versus residual networks, batch normalization, depth-related training error, and the cited special initialization methods.
Comparisons of initialization methods, training speed, and trainable depth.

The experiments use online gradient descent on 500 fixed training examples for one or ten epochs, rather than the stated wide-network squared-loss recipe. They do not report a transient initial loss rise followed by low training loss, nor sharpness tracking over longer full-batch training.
Batch-normalization comparisons and Fixup training without normalization.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Online gradient descent on Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR10, varied depth and learning rate
reader_labels.reason: The authors report that the η = 2/L prediction coincided with the boundary of accuracy collapse and that loss reduced in the areas beyond the boundary (R1–R8). These results are consistent in part with a learning-rate boundary, but do not establish the stated transient-rise-then-low-training-loss pattern.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Learning rates beyond the stated boundary in the small online-training experiments
reader_labels.reason: Accuracy did not improve in the above-boundary region despite reduced loss, and the authors report only slight testing-loss boundary violation at large depth (R1–R8).
